key_insight: RefVFX transfer complex, dynamic visual effects from a reference video onto a target video or image in a single feed-forward pass, without per-instance tuning, while preserving content and temporal coherence.
problem_solved: Existing editing approaches struggle to reproduce rich temporal effects (e.g., dynamic lighting, character transformations) that are hard to describe via text or static keyframes; RefVFX enables direct transfer of those temporal dynamics between videos/images without expensive per-video fine-tuning.
method: Encode temporal effect dynamics from a reference video into a transferable representation that captures motion, lighting and transformation cues.
Apply a feed-forward, tuning-free transfer mechanism that modulates the target video/image with the encoded temporal dynamics at inference time.
Enforce temporal consistency and content preservation so the transferred effect remains coherent across frames and keeps target identity/structure intact.
impact: Makes realistic, temporally consistent visual-effect transfer practical and fast for creators and ML practitioners—reducing manual keyframing and per-instance training, and enabling scalable VFX workflows and rapid prototyping.
visual_elements: Before / After video strip: reference video, target input, and resulting output side-by-side to show transferred dynamics.
Simplified architecture block diagram: Reference encoder -> Transfer/modulation module -> Temporal consistency check -> Output.
Temporal dynamics visualization: timelines or flow overlays showing how lighting/motion patterns are extracted from reference and applied to target.
Comparison chart: accuracy/temporal coherence vs. prior prompt/keyframe or fine-tuning methods and a latency/throughput bar for tuning-free inference.
paper_title: Tuning-free Visual Effect Transfer across Videos
paper_authors: Maxwell Jones, Rameen Abdal, Or Patashnik, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Sergey Tulyakov
